chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sindi narrated to me from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibrahim ibn Mi'zam al-Asadi, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

Indeed, the tongue of the son of Adam overlooks all its limbs every day and says: 'How have you fared?' They say: 'In good condition, if you spare us.' They say: 'Allah, Allah [be merciful] to us,' and they implore him, and say: 'We are rewarded only because of you, and punished only because of you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the role of the tongue in relation to the body's reward and punishment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this vivid metaphor from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) personifies the tongue as the chief negotiator for the body's limbs, arguing that since all actions are executed through it, the ultimate reward or punishment rests upon its testimony. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the tongue as the primary instrument of *Amal* (action), linking verbal declaration directly to divine accountability. It serves as a practical reminder for believers to guard their speech, as the tongue effectively vouches for the integrity of the entire physical self before God.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam  Zainul  Abideen  (a.s.)  said,  “The  human  tongue does a favor on other parts of the body every day. It inquires about their condition. The parts of body say: If you spare us, we  will  remain  in  good  condition.  They  beg  for  Allah’s mercy and say that if they are rewarded, it is because of the tongue and if they are punished, it is also because of the tongue.”
